doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Parents' Alabama background and their music
summary: His parents came from Birmingham; his father attended an industrial school and sang; his mother was a trained pianist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I’m curious if your parents were — did they feel good about you pursuing music as a career?

Well it’s kind of tragic in a way. See my mother and father, they’re from Birmingham, Alabama. And my grandparents on his side, they own land, and they worked the land, and also from what I understand they would provide seed and fertilizer, and then the neighbors, they would all sharecrop and then they’d split the proceeds. And my dad, let’s see I had three aunts and two uncles, and so my dad, they sent him to an industrial school in Tennessee, which later I guess became part of the school system, the college system down there.
